lines.head: The job
sentences: A fall from a ladder, onto the decking.
He hit his head, and he was out for two minutes.
His family helped him inside.
Now he's at the kitchen table.
All he wants to talk about is his hip.
His neck's fine, he says.
So, is it?

lines.head: Two reasons
sentences: The spinal injury protocol gives two reasons for spinal precautions.
Spinal pain, tenderness, neck ache or back pain.
Or a mechanism that could injure the spine.
Think about an injury above the chest.
Or a distracting injury.
Either one is enough.

lines.head: His red flags
sentences: Look at what he's got.
A fall from more than one metre.
A head strike, with loss of consciousness.
A painful hip that's taking all his attention.
He's concussed, and he can't remember the fall.
And he's 67.
With any of these, don't try to clear his neck.
His answer can't be relied on.

lines.head: He's already walked
sentences: He's already walked inside.
Don't let him do it again.
Explain why, and hold his head still.
No mobility assessment.
Check for paralysis, tingling, weakness or numbness, and for low blood pressure.
Any of those?
Request clinical support, and use the vacuum mattress.

lines.head: Towel roll, not a collar
sentences: Which technique?
After a knock-out, there are concerns about raised pressure in the head.
That rules out a semi-rigid collar.
Use a modified towel roll.
Two towels, two saline bags, and tape across the forehead.
Never tape the head to the stretcher.
And no long board.

lines.head: The move
sentences: Plan the move from the chair to the stretcher as a team.
Keep the head and spine in line.
Keep movement to a minimum.
Methoxyflurane can help with a short, painful move like this.

lines.head: Pain and nausea
sentences: For the hip, think multimodal.
Paracetamol.
Ibuprofen, if it's safe.
Methoxyflurane.
A ketamine wafer?
Not on the protocol alone.
He's concussed, and he's over 64.
Feeling sick?
Ondansetron can be given before transport after head or spine trauma, when vomiting would be risky.

lines.head: Hand over
sentences: Put the C-spine NOT clear sticker on him.
Record your decisions on the PCR.
At handover, say why his neck isn't cleared.
He walked in.
He still needs the precautions.
